# Native solver source and license provenance

The version, upstream URL, and exact source-archive SHA-256 for every dependency are recorded in `third_party/SOLVER_DEPS.json`. License and notice files in the versioned directories are copied verbatim from those verified archives, preserving upstream relative paths.

The Boost.Serialization component archive does not contain the common Boost license text. `boost-serialization-1.74.0/LICENSE_1_0.txt` contains the BSL-1.0 license paragraph from the installed Ubuntu 22.04 `/usr/share/doc/libboost1.74-dev/copyright`, with Debian copyright-format indentation and blank-line markers removed. Copyright statements remain in the original Boost.Serialization source archive.

The bootstrap retains all five original, unmodified source archives, the pinned manifest, and the bootstrap itself under its local prefix's `share/tiger-sheets/sources`. It copies these license texts and upstream notices under `share/tiger-sheets/licenses/solvers`. The small Boost.Serialization CMake wrapper is generated by the preserved bootstrap; it does not alter the original source archive. System Boost 1.74 headers are a documented build prerequisite.

HiGHS and NLopt are linked statically. NLopt is built with `NLOPT_LUKSAN=OFF`; the preserved source archive also contains disabled algorithms and their original license notices. pagmo, oneTBB, and Boost.Serialization are linked as shared libraries. pagmo is built with `$ORIGIN` as its installed runtime search path so its companion shared libraries can be replaced in the same installation directory. Keep the source and license directories with release artifacts.
